disclaimer: This report is for educational and wellness purposes only. It is not a medical diagnosis and does not replace advice from a qualified healthcare professional. HbA1c results should be confirmed by your doctor. Do not start, stop or change any medication without medical advice.

status.label: In the prediabetes range
status.explanation: Your HbA1c is between 5.7% and 6.4%, the range used for prediabetes. This is a common and often reversible stage where lifestyle changes make the biggest difference.

summary: Your HbA1c of 5.7 falls in the prediabetes range, which means your blood sugar is a bit higher than ideal but there is good opportunity to change course. Carrying extra body weight, drinking alcohol regularly, being over 45, and having high cholesterol or triglycerides all add to your overall risk. The most valuable next steps are keeping up with your lipid profile and HbA1c checks, staying active regularly, and following the food guidance around saturated fat and fibre to support both blood sugar and cholesterol.

risk_factors.label: Body weight above the healthy range
Existing health condition: High cholesterol or triglycerides

comorbidity_assessment.note: High cholesterol and triglycerides often travel together with higher blood sugar, and both can affect heart and blood vessel health over time. Managing fat intake and staying active can help support both your lipid levels and your blood sugar.

constraints: Keep saturated fat low (limit ghee, butter, coconut oil, red and processed meat); avoid trans fats (vanaspati, many fried and bakery foods).
Include soluble fibre daily (oats, barley, pulses, psyllium) and unsaturated fats (nuts, seeds, olive or mustard oil in small amounts).

foods_to_eat: Legumes such as lentils, chickpeas and beans
Fatty fish like salmon and sardines
Nuts and seeds such as walnuts, almonds and flaxseed
Whole grains like quinoa and brown rice
foods_to_avoid: Pastries, cakes and other bakery items made with refined flour
Processed and red meat such as sausages and bacon
Fried foods and items cooked in vanaspati or hydrogenated oils
Butter, ghee and coconut oil in large amounts
Sweets, candy and desserts high in added sugar
White bread and other refined grain products
plan.portion_guidance: Aim for a palm-sized portion of protein, a fist-sized portion of whole grains, and fill half your plate with non-starchy vegetables at lunch and dinner. Use measuring cups or your hand as a guide to keep portions consistent with your 1,850 kcal target.
plan.hydration: Drink plenty of water through the day, aim for 8 to 10 glasses. Limit sugary drinks and keep alcohol intake modest, choosing water or unsweetened tea between drinks if you do drink.
based_on: high cholesterol or triglycerides: low saturated fat, more soluble fibre and unsaturated fats
regular alcohol use: hydration guidance included

exercise: Begin with brisk walking or cycling for 20-30 minutes, 4-5 days a week, gradually building to at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity weekly. Aerobic activity like this helps improve HDL cholesterol and triglyceride levels over time.
Add simple strength exercises, such as bodyweight squats, resistance bands, or light weights, on 2 non-consecutive days a week.
Include a 5-10 minute warm-up and cool-down with each session to protect joints and ease into higher activity levels safely.
lifestyle.walking_goal: Start with 20 minutes of walking most days this week, then build up to at least 30 minutes a day, 5 days a week, over the next month.
lifestyle.weight_management: Since your BMI falls in the overweight range, gradually working toward a modest reduction in body weight through consistent activity and balanced eating habits can help improve your HbA1c and cholesterol levels over time. Aim for slow, steady progress rather than quick changes.
lifestyle.sleep: Aim for 7-9 hours of sleep each night. Try to keep a consistent bedtime and wake time, limit screens for an hour before bed, and keep your bedroom cool, dark, and quiet to support restful sleep.
stress: Practice slow, deep breathing for 5-10 minutes daily, such as inhaling for 4 counts and exhaling for 6 counts, to help calm your nervous system.
Try progressive muscle relaxation or a short guided meditation before bed to ease tension built up during the day.
Consider setting aside time each week for an enjoyable hobby or social activity, since this can lower stress and support healthier habits overall.
behaviour_change: Since you drink regularly, consider cutting back gradually, for example by setting alcohol-free days each week and tracking your intake, as reducing alcohol can support healthier triglyceride and blood sugar levels.
Build small, sustainable habits one at a time, such as adding a daily walk before working on strength training, to make lasting change easier.
Keep track of your progress with a simple journal or app to stay motivated and notice patterns between habits and how you feel.
based_on: Aerobic activity benefits for HDL cholesterol and triglycerides

monitoring.name: Lipid profile (cholesterol)
monitoring.why: Diabetes and high cholesterol together raise the risk of heart disease and stroke.
monitoring.frequency: Every year (at least every 5 years if you are under 40), or as your doctor advises
risk_indicators: Existing cholesterol problem or heart disease

monitoring.name: HbA1c
monitoring.why: Catches progression from prediabetes to diabetes early.

monitoring.name: Fasting blood sugar
monitoring.why: Shows your blood glucose after an overnight fast and complements HbA1c.
monitoring.frequency: Alongside your HbA1c test, or as your doctor advises

monitoring.name: Blood pressure
monitoring.why: High blood pressure multiplies the heart and kidney risks of high blood glucose.
monitoring.frequency: At every doctor visit; at home regularly if you have high blood pressure

preventive_actions: Schedule a lipid profile test since it is highlighted as a priority for you.
Aim for regular aerobic activity most days of the week to help improve cholesterol and support blood sugar control.
Follow the suggested calorie target of 1850 calories a day to support a healthy weight.
Reduce saturated fat sources like ghee, butter, coconut oil, and processed meat, and avoid trans fats from fried or bakery foods.
Add soluble fibre foods like oats, barley, pulses, and psyllium to your daily meals.
Consider cutting back on regular alcohol use, as it can affect both blood sugar and triglyceride levels.

hba1c_caveat: HbA1c can be less accurate if you have anaemia, kidney disease, a recent blood transfusion or certain haemoglobin variants.
